transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose it’s the driving, really—though I’ve driven my whole life, you know, and my late husband used to say I was the steadier one on the road. But lately, when my car gets to one of those long bridges toward Miami, it’s like it happens all at once. My chest tightens, my hands just clamp down on the steering wheel, and I get this awful sudden certainty that I have to get off right then… even though, of course, there’s nowhere to go on a bridge. That’s what finally made me come in.
Have you ever had similar feelings of chest tightness and sudden fear in situations other than when you’re on the bridge driving?

It’s really the bridges, doctor—those long ones on the way toward Miami. I mean, I’ve been in nervous situations before like anyone, but what made me come in is that the second my car gets onto one of those bridges, my chest tightens right up and my hands clamp down on the wheel. I get this sudden feeling that I have to get off immediately, which is silly because of course there’s nowhere to go. My husband used to tease me about taking the scenic route, though that was more because I liked looking at the water, not this awful feeling.
Have you ever experienced sudden feelings of intense fear or panic in situations other than driving on bridges, like in crowds, while exercising, or when you're alone at home?

No, not really in those other places—not like that. I can be uneasy here and there, I mean at my age you notice things more, and crowds can be tiresome, especially when people don’t look where they’re going with those carts in the market. But the real sudden fear is when my car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami. It’s almost immediate—my chest tightens, my hands grab the wheel, and I feel absolutely sure I need to get off right then, even though there’s nowhere to go.
When you're not on the bridge, do you ever experience sudden attacks of intense fear that come out of the blue, even when there’s no immediate danger?

I don’t think so… not out of the blue like that. I mean, I can get startled—anyone can, especially when the phone rings during supper, and my neighbor has this dog that barks at absolutely nothing—but that isn’t the same thing, is it? The real trouble I notice is tied to those bridges. Otherwise I can’t say I’ve had those sudden attacks just sitting at home or anything.
Have you ever had an episode where your heart raced, you felt short of breath, or you thought something terrible was going to happen, even when you weren’t anywhere near a bridge?

Well… not really away from the bridge, no. I mean, I can get myself worked up about little things—my sister says I fuss over traffic like it’s a personal insult—but the thing that made me come in is very specific. The moment my car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami, my chest tightens, my hands just clamp onto the wheel, and I get this sudden certainty that I have to get off right then… even though, of course, there’s nowhere to go.
Because of this fear on the bridges, do you find yourself avoiding driving on them altogether, taking different routes, or does someone else have to drive instead?

Yes… I have started avoiding them, more than I like to admit. I’ll turn down things I used to enjoy—gallery openings, birdwatching outings, even visiting my daughter sometimes—unless someone else can drive me across those bridges. And that embarrasses me, honestly, because I’ve always been the one who made the plans and handled everything myself.

Have you ever had sudden attacks of intense fear with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like something terrible is happening, even when you weren’t near a bridge or driving at all?

I’m trying to think… no, I don’t believe I’ve had that just out of nowhere. Not sitting at home or in the grocery store or something like that. I mean, I do get flustered—who doesn’t at my age, especially when people rush you in parking lots—but the kind of fear you’re describing, I only really connect it with the bridge situation.
